# Story Package: Joseph and His Coat (Genesis 37)

**Story Key**: `josephCoat`

**Position in 365 Roadmap**: Phase 1, Story #5 — God’s care even when family hurts us.

---

## Reverent Read-Aloud Retelling (for ages 3–8)

Jacob had twelve sons, but he loved Joseph more than the others. He made Joseph a beautiful coat with many colors. When Joseph’s brothers saw the coat, they became very jealous.

One day Joseph had two special dreams. In the dreams, his brothers and even his parents bowed down to him. When he told his family about the dreams, his brothers hated him even more.

One day the brothers were far away taking care of the sheep. Jacob sent Joseph to check on them. When the brothers saw Joseph coming, they made a bad plan. They took his beautiful coat away and threw him into a deep pit. Later they sold him to some traders who were going to Egypt.

The brothers dipped Joseph’s coat in goat’s blood and took it home to their father. Jacob thought a wild animal had hurt Joseph and he was very, very sad.

But God was still with Joseph, even in Egypt. He had a special plan for Joseph’s life, even though his brothers had been mean to him.

---

## Coloring Page Prompt

Simple black-and-white line art for ages 3–8. A young boy wearing a colorful striped coat. Several older brothers looking jealous. A deep empty pit nearby. In the background, traders with camels. Calm but sad feeling. Clean bold lines, large open spaces.

---

## Read-Along Flow

Color the colorful coat and the sad moment → listen to how God stays with us even when family or friends hurt us → hope that God has good plans even in hard times.

## Quiz — 4 Questions (with helpful scaffolding)

**1. Why did Joseph’s brothers become jealous of him?**
- A) Because he was the oldest
- B) Because their father gave him a beautiful colorful coat and loved him more
- C) Because he was stronger than them
- D) Because he had more sheep

*Correct: B*  
Wrong answers scaffolding:
- If A: “Joseph wasn’t the oldest. The coat and extra love from their father made the brothers jealous.”
- If C: “The story doesn’t say he was stronger. It was the special coat and their father’s love.”
- If D: “It wasn’t about sheep. Their father showed Joseph special favor with the coat.”

**2. What did the brothers do with Joseph’s beautiful coat?**
- A) They washed it for him
- B) They took it away and later dipped it in blood to trick their father
- C) They tore it into pieces and threw it away
- D) They gave it to their father

*Correct: B*  
Wrong answers scaffolding:
- If A: “They didn’t wash it. They took it from him when they sold him.”
- If C: “They kept the coat and used it to lie to their father by putting blood on it.”
- If D: “They used the coat to make their father think Joseph was dead.”

**3. Even after his brothers were mean to him, who stayed with Joseph?**
- A) His brothers
- B) God
- C) His father Jacob
- D) No one

*Correct: B*  
Wrong answers scaffolding:
- If A: “His brothers had been cruel. But God never left Joseph, even when he was taken far away to Egypt.”
- If C: “Jacob was very sad and thought Joseph was dead. God was the One who stayed close to Joseph.”
- If D: “God was always with Joseph. He had good plans even in the hard times.”

**4. What does this story help us remember when people we love hurt us?**
- A) That we should hurt them back
- B) That God can still have good plans for us and will never leave us
- C) That we should never trust anyone
- D) That dreams always come true right away

*Correct: B*  
Wrong answers scaffolding:
- If A: “Hurting people back is not God’s way. Joseph’s story shows God can bring good even from bad things.”
- If C: “We can still trust God even when people disappoint us. He stays with us.”
- If D: “The dreams did come true later, but not right away. God’s timing is perfect.”
